description: Unified state-kill ledger: every kill normalized to the canonical state key, deduped across sources, all attributions retained, counted once.

canonical_key_spec.phase_d: (window, a_t, b, branch, d2_zero, sigma_zero, g_zero_levels, deg_d1, deg_d2, deg_e, deg_sigma)
canonical_key_spec.column: (column, target_window, cellname) -- a whole (a_t, b, branch) column emptied by a frontier stage lemma; NOT a raw phase-D state, excluded from the per-state census, and carrying the flag-case/state counts it covers (computed from the universe)

totals.phase_d_state_coverage_note: in_universe = enumerated degree-states; killed_per_state = individual kill records; covered_by_column = states inside a cell emptied by a frontier stage lemma (frontier_rebuild.STAGES); covered_either = union; uncovered = neither. The two buckets overlap heavily and MUST NOT be added. *** READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING uncovered. *** uncovered > 0 in THIS artifact does NOT mean those states are alive. The `e | Phi` divisor lemma is OPT-IN here (--divisor-filter, see the top of this file), and it is what kills them: in state_kill_ledger_divfilter.json uncovered is 0 in BOTH windows, i.e. all 52005 enumerated states are dead. proof_dag.py recomputes the divisor lemma's cell-level consequences directly and therefore closes both f31 windows regardless of which ledger variant it was built from -- so a nonzero uncovered here and a CLOSED subcase:sub1/sub2 in proof_dag.json are consistent, not contradictory.
totals.phase_d_state_coverage_full_pipeline: the number to quote for frontier coverage is the one from `python state_kill_ledger.py --divisor-filter`, which applies the compiler's authoritative pipeline (e|Phi, then the stages). FRONTIER_REBUILD.md sec.1 calls that the authoritative compile.
